newsitem.title: CANADA: Teck says hopes for mine at Petaquilla.
newsitem.headline: Teck says hopes for mine at Petaquilla.

text.p: Teck Corp said Wednesday that it believes the Petaquilla copper-gold property in Panama will ultimately be proven to have the makings of a mine if market factors are favorable.
"I think this is going to make a mine in due course. It's going to take hard work to get it there," Teck president Norman Keevil said in an interview.
Teck has an option to acquire a 26 percent stake in the project from Adrian Resources Ltd which currently has 52 percent while Inmet Mining Corp has 48 percent.
Adrian was at odds with its partners after a feasibility study done last year by Teck led Teck and Inmet to conclude a production commitment was not advisable in current conditions.
Adrian and Teck reached agreement Wednesday on work intended to improve project economics and develop a final bankable feasability study by next January.

Keevil and an Adrian spokesman said the deal resolved their differences. "We're happy we reached an agreement with Teck," the Adrian spokesman said. "The goal is to head towards a completed final feasbility study...We've been confident we are going to have a mine all along."

Adrian had put Petaquilla's proven reserves at 1.46 billion tonnes of ore containing 13.74 billion pounds of copper and 3.17 million ounces of gold. Adrian said Teck's numbers were lower but were not released.

Keevil said the dispute centered on the use of different ore search paramters around drill holes by consultants for the two companies. But he said "from a practical point of view it doesnt make too much difference" because despite the discrepancy the deposit "is still very large."
"We've agreed to include both sets of parameters in the (upcoming) study and let the readers take their choice."

"The fact of the matter is that (Petaquilla) is about 60 percent higher grade than Highland Valley Copper and bigger. It's in that class only bigger, higher grade, and Highland Valley is a very good mine. It's a matter of engineering it into production at the right time," Keevil said.
The Highland Valley copper mine in British Columbia is owned by Teck, Cominco Ltd and Rio Algom Ltd.

A final decision will "depend on the copper market, on smelting terms, a whole bunch of things. But I certainly hope at some point we put it in (to production) because it's a very major resource," Keevil said.
